_tx.description: A committed transaction, read from the journal: one call to apply(), whose bundles all committed together.

seq.description: its place in the journal's total order, the cursor a feed holds

via.description: the session, connector or other entity it was made through

_change.description: One component a transaction wrote or removed, read from the journal.

comp.description: the component it wrote or removed; entity for a deletion

component.description: that component's name, which a graph that does not describe its vocabulary as _comp rows reads in place of comp

value.description: the properties it wrote; absent where it removed the component

kept.description: what the store's file kept on one UTC day, measured once that day from its page statistics, so history can be read against the rest of the file: the file's bytes, how many of them were free, each table's bytes with its indexes and its rows, and the changes the journal held per component. History is the journal's tables (`journal_*`) and each component's versions (`<comp>$versions`)

free.description: how many of them were free pages

file.description: the file it measured, where the store keeps one on a disk

tables.description: by table: [bytes, rows], its indexes' bytes folded into its own

changes.description: by component name: the changes the journal held for it, a deletion's under entity; absent where the store keeps no journal

history.title: Read an entity’s history
history.description: List every committed transaction that touched one entity, newest first. Each is returned as the patch it applied (the named groups of fields it wrote, or $delete if it deleted the record) stamped with `_tx`: the transaction's place in the journal (`seq`), when it committed (`at`), whom it acted for (`by`) and through what (`via`). The journal is written inside the same transaction as the batch, so this gives attribution and a diff without a version table. It covers changes made since this graph started journaling.

entity.description: record whose history to read: human-readable id, registered name, or unique entity id (eid)

limit.description: return at most this many transactions, counting back from the newest

branch_new.title: Make a branch
branch_new.description: Fork the whole graph at main's newest transaction; nothing is copied. Answers the branch: its id, the transaction it forked at (fork) and when. Pass the id as branch to graph_query, graph_show and graph_apply to read and write on it; main never sees its writes, and they reach no effect. Needs @yaks/journal with versions on.

branch_list.title: List branches
branch_list.description: Active branches of the graph, oldest first: id, the transaction of main it forked at (fork) and when it was made. Pass trash to list trashed branches, including when each was trashed.

trash.description: List trashed branches instead of active ones.

branch_delete.title: Trash a branch
branch_delete.description: Move a branch to trash; every version written on it stays recoverable and main is untouched. Answers the trashed branch. Use branch_list with trash to find it and branch_restore to return it. Nothing is permanently erased.

id.description: The branch's id, as branch_new and branch_list give it.

branch_restore.title: Restore a branch
branch_restore.description: Return a trashed branch with every version written on it. Answers the active branch. Find its id with branch_list and trash.

id.description: The branch's id, as branch_new and branch_list give it.

branch_merge.title: Merge a branch into main
branch_merge.description: Write what a branch changed since its fork to main as one batch. Each property merges against its value at the fork: one only the branch changed takes the branch's value, one only main changed keeps main's. A property both changed to different values is a conflict, and nothing merges by itself: while any conflict has no pick, nothing is written, and the answer lists the conflicts, each with its value at the fork, on the branch and on main side by side. Pass a pick for each to merge. A removed component or deleted entity against the other side's edit is a conflict too. Answers the conflicts left and the bundles written; the branch is left as it is.

id.description: The branch's id, as branch_new and branch_list give it.

pick.description: Which value each conflict takes: its eid, comp and prop as the conflicts list them, and take, branch or main.

main.description: The value main held as the conflict listed it. A main that has moved since is one the pick never saw, so the conflict stands again.

_tx.description: A committed transaction, read from the journal: one call to apply(), whose bundles all committed together.

_change.description: One component a transaction wrote or removed, read from the journal.
